title: The Regenokine Registry: An open, real-world database investigating the incidence, safety and efficacy of cell-free autologous conditioned serum (ACS) in the treatment of pain conditions. A project of the Orthogen Study Group (OSG) and the Research Network of Autologous Conditioned Serum users, carried out in cooperation with the Canadian Research Chair in Human Pain Genetics and other corporate partners
summary:
Chronic pain that impairs quality of life affects one-fifth of the world's population. Unlike acute pain, chronic pain often lasts longer than expected and frequently has no obvious cause. Possible causes include musculoskeletal disorders, nerve pain, autoimmune diseases and psychological factors. Chronic pain is the most common cause of disability and represents a significant economic burden. Those affected not only experience physical discomfort, but also have limited freedom of movement and reduced ability to perform. They are also often affected by mental health issues such as depression and anxiety. Currently, chronic pain treatment relies heavily on pharmacological agents. While these provide some relief, they are often only partially effective and are associated with side effects. Furthermore, the suppression of the inflammatory response by corticosteroids or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs may increase the risk of developing a chronic condition.
This registry aims to expand existing knowledge about diagnostic and therapeutic pathways for patients who routinely receive cell-free autologous conditioned serum (ACS), either alone or in combination with other treatments. Particular attention is paid to the safety of the various treatment options.

interventions.name: This research project is not a study in itself, but rather a process of collecting data as part of creating a registry.  No additional measures or examinations will be carried out beyond those that form part of routine clinical practice.
